mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP growth rate indicates a growing economy, which leads to higher consumer spending and increased demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances with strong GDP growth, or GDP growth rate does not lead to increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 4.5% signals an easing monetary cycle, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 5% indicates a slowing economy, leading to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances with high unemployment rate, or unemployment rate does not lead to decreased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances with high industrial production, or industrial production does not lead to increased economic activity.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high GDP growth rate and low unemployment rate indicates a strong economy, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances with strong GDP growth and low unemployment, or the combination of GDP growth and unemployment rate does not lead to increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate and an increase in the money supply indicate an easing monetary cycle, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a growing economy, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances with high payroll employment, or payroll employment does not lead to increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high housing starts and low unemployment rate indicates a strong economy, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances with high housing starts and low unemployment, or the combination of housing starts and unemployment rate does not lead to increased consumer spending.
